episodes.tag: Liquid Cooling, Data Center of the Future
episodes.title: Data Center News Show - Feb 26, 2026
episodes.description: We discussed liquid cooling solutions solving the water usage problem of data centers and the data center of the future.  The participants highlight a critical transition toward liquid cooling systems, which are necessary to manage the extreme heat generated by modern artificial intelligence hardware. Beyond cooling, the conversation explores the urgent need for energy independence, suggesting that developers may soon bypass traditional power grids to build private nuclear or fusion capabilities. The experts also address common public misconceptions regarding water usage, explaining how closed-loop systems significantly reduce environmental impact. Ultimately, the source emphasizes that operational efficiency and technological growth in the sector now depend on integrating advanced thermodynamics and sustainable power solutions.

episodes.title: Data Center News Show - February 19, 2026
episodes.description: This discussion highlights the current state of the **data center industry**, focusing on the **public misinformation** and **community resistance** surrounding large-scale developments. episodes.tag: Nuclear power, Grid Infrastructure, High-Density Computing
episodes.title: Data Center News Show - February 12, 2026
episodes.description: This episode of the Data Center News Show examines the critical infrastructure shifts necessary to support the rise of artificial intelligence and high-density computing. A major focus is the essential transition from air cooling to liquid cooling systems, which provide significantly better heat rejection for modern GPUs and a typical return on investment of about 21 months. The panel clarifies misconceptions about water usage, noting that the industry is moving away from evaporative towers toward closed-loop systems and reclaimed water sources. Faced with power grid wait times as long as ten years, developers are increasingly pursuing power independence by collocating data centers with nuclear plants and exploring the potential of Small Modular Reactors. Additionally, the conversation highlights how transitioning from AC to DC power architectures and utilizing liquid-cooled transformers can dramatically improve energy efficiency, eventually allowing waste heat to be repurposed via absorption cooling technology.

episodes.title: Data Center News Show - January 29, 2026
episodes.description: On this Data Center News Show, we feature industry experts to explore a projected $3 trillion "investment super cycle" driven by the global demand for AI and GPU-dense environments. The panel recaps the latest insights from the PTC conference, highlighting a shift toward a more democratized workforce while addressing the acute labor shortage that currently hinders rapid growth. To combat these hurdles, the guests emphasize the importance of trade-based education, community college certificate programs, and the need for companies to move more decisively when hiring talent. The conversation also tackles the rise of "NIMBYism" and community resistance, advocating for a stronger public relations effort to demystify data centers as clean, tax-positive operators that improve local infrastructure. Finally, the episode dives into the future of facility management, showcasing how robotics and IoT sensors are revolutionizing the industry by enabling predictive maintenance and augmenting staff for high-stakes tasks like thermal imaging and equipment monitoring.

episodes.title: Data Center News Show - January 22, 2026
episodes.description: In this transcript from the Data Center News Show, industry experts discuss the critical infrastructure and power challenges currently facing the data center sector. Andy Urda from LS Electric highlights the expansion of domestic manufacturing for circuit breakers and switchgear to resolve supply chain delays, while Wyatt Pemberton of Critical Grid Solutions examines the shift toward on-site power generation and "behind-the-fence" solutions to bypass grid congestion. The conversation explores technical transitions, such as moving toward high-efficiency DC power and the rising demand for AI-driven compute density. Additionally, the participants address the public relations hurdles of the industry, emphasizing the need for better community engagement regarding noise, water use, and emissions. Ultimately, the source provides a comprehensive look at how technological innovation and decentralized energy are being used to meet the explosive growth of digital infrastructure.

episodes.title: Data Center News Show - January 15, 2026
episodes.description: In this episode, we celebrate the first anniversary of the Data Center News Show - focused on data center industry news. The discussion features experts from Supermicro and the Nomad Futurist Foundation, who offer practical advice for attending the Pacific Telecommunications Council (PTC) conference in Hawaii. A significant portion of the conversation addresses the critical power shortage facing the industry, noting that massive energy demands for AI infrastructure are outpacing utility capabilities. The participants explore technical solutions like liquid cooling and onsite power generation while lamenting the long wait times for grid connections. Finally, the group emphasizes the need for better public relations to counter negative perceptions of data centers and highlight their role in driving the global economy.

episodes.title: Data Center News Show - January 8, 2026
episodes.description: In this episode of the show, industry experts discuss the rapid evolution of the AI race and its impact on infrastructure, specifically dismissing claims that edge devices will replace data centers as a "hallucination." Instead, they highlight a shift toward autonomous agents and unstructured data, which is driving a massive need for "adaptive reuse"—repurposing industrial sites like paper plants and steel mills into GPU-ready facilities in as little as six to nine months. The panel emphasizes the high profitability of GPU-as-a-service for the mid-market and contrasts Pennsylvania’s supportive regulatory environment with the rising "NIMBYism" and moratoriums seen in other regions. To maintain a competitive edge over China’s R&D pace, the experts suggest the U.S. leverage Small Modular Reactors (SMRs) and strategic nuclear fuel reserves to power the next generation of sites. Looking toward 2026, the discussion predicts a $3 trillion "investment super cycle" defined by the standard use of data center robots, modular construction, and the emergence of ultra-high-density one-megawatt racks to maximize speed and profitability.

episodes.tag: Energy, Grid Infrastructure, Behind the Meter
episodes.title: Data Center News Show - December 18, 2025
episodes.description: In this episode, we feature industry experts analyzing the shift toward on-site power generation as a solution to grid congestion and long utility lead times. The panel explores the benefits of fuel cells and modular infrastructure, emphasizing that generating power behind the meter can improve a data center's speed to market and financial predictability. Participants highlight the potential for heat reuse and liquid cooling to increase efficiency, though they acknowledge that high capital costs and supply chain bottlenecks remain significant hurdles. Looking toward 2035, the experts predict a future defined by increased modularity, deeper community engagement through technical education, and the possible emergence of space-based facilities. Ultimately, the source underscores a transition toward energy independence as operators navigate political pressures and the rising demands of artificial intelligence.

episodes.title: Data Center News Show - December 11, 2025
episodes.description: In this episode, I discuss several topics with industry expert, Martin Renkis.  We discuss the evolving landscape of digital infrastructure, specifically focusing on the upcoming PTC conference and the unique business dynamics of the data center sector. They explore the critical shift toward on-site power generation necessitated by massive utility grid backlogs and the rising energy demands of artificial intelligence. The conversation highlights technical innovations in cooling methods, such as liquid and immersion systems, which are becoming essential as traditional air cooling struggles to manage high-density racks. Furthermore, they address the logistical hurdles of land acquisition and power studies, while emphasizing the industry's need for better public education regarding environmental impact and community benefits. Together, they provide a snapshot of an industry grappling with rapid growth, specialized labor shortages, and the complexities of building sustainable, high-capacity facilities.

Tune in and stay informed—your competitive edge depends on it.

episodes.title: Data Center News Show - November 13, 2025
episodes.description: On this episode of the Data Center News Show, we feature a group of industry experts discussing the rapid expansion and logistical hurdles of modern data infrastructure. A primary focus is the massive power demand in Texas, where interconnection requests have reached staggering levels despite concerns about project viability and water scarcity. The participants explore how on-site power generation and liquid cooling technologies are becoming essential as traditional utility grids struggle to keep pace with high-density AI workloads. We also critique the current state of OpenAI, debating the company's financial stability and its recent calls for government loan backing. Furthermore, the conversation highlights the collaborative nature of the data center community and the urgent need for better public advocacy to counter negative industry perceptions. Together, the speakers suggest that while the sector faces significant capital and resource constraints, it remains a critical engine for technological growth.

episodes.title: Data Center News Show - October 9, 2025
episodes.description: In this episode, we discuss the evolving infrastructure of the digital world. The participants address public concerns regarding surging energy costs, clarifying that data center power consumption is often overshadowed by residential cooling needs. A significant portion of the conversation focuses on AI-driven densification, highlighting how new hardware from companies like Nvidia is forcing a shift toward advanced liquid cooling solutions. The panel also explores the financial landscape of the industry, noting that massive investments from firms like BlackRock signal that data centers are now viewed as stable, mature assets. Finally, the experts debate the operational risks of packing too much power into single server racks, suggesting a future need for balanced, distributed designs.

episodes.title: Data Center News Show - October 2, 2025
episodes.description: This episode features a roundtable discussion regarding the rapid evolution of digital infrastructure driven by the AI hype cycle. Industry experts debate the AI efficiency paradox, questioning whether increased hardware performance will eventually lead to a market glut or if society’s insatiable appetite for data will sustain growth. The participants examine the practicalities of modular data center deployments and the necessity of retrofitting existing urban buildings to support high-density power requirements. They also explore the tensions between speed of innovation and environmental sustainability, noting that the competitive "arms race" often prioritizes operational capacity over green energy goals. Additional topics include the rise of open-source AI models like DeepSeek and the unique distributed compute strategies currently being utilized within the defense sector. Ultimately, the panel highlights how advanced liquid cooling and prefabricated designs are essential tools for adapting to an unpredictable technological future.
